text: Agile methodology is a popular approach to project management, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at the start, teams work in short, focused periods called sprints, usually lasting two to four weeks. Each day begins with a brief standup meeting, where everyone shares what they did yesterday and what they will do today. Before starting a sprint, the team selects tasks from a detailed list called a backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, describing a feature from the perspective of the end user. This iterative development process allows teams to adapt quickly to changes, test ideas regularly, and deliver small, valuable updates frequently.
